row.evidence: Userpilot's SCIM guide says 'This feature is available on the Enterprise plan and requires SSO to be enabled'; the pricing page lists SAML 2.0 SSO and Advanced User Management only on Enterprise (Let's Talk).
row.notes: SCIM (directory sync via an SSO setup portal, group-to-role mapping) is Enterprise only and requires SSO, also Enterprise only; JIT is Enterprise too. SCIM 'User deleted' removes the teammate from the organization; removal from all mapped groups removes them from that application. While SCIM is on, SSO is mandatory and manual invites/CSV import are disabled. No SCIM base URL, token or endpoint list is published (set up through the portal), so generic is null. Pricing is flat per account by MAU: Starter $299/mo (3 seats), Growth from $849/mo (15 seats), Enterprise custom (unlimited); the page shows no annual/monthly toggle. The public HTTP API covers end-users, companies and events, not teammates. No Okta OIN or Entra gallery app found.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.notes: Access and activity logs in the UI; no audit-log API documented.

auth.token_source: Settings > Team > Authentication > Directory sync (SCIM) card, Setup SCIM (setup portal)

operations.notes: Documented as directory events (user added to/removed from group, user updated, user deleted, group created/deleted), not as SCIM HTTP operations; update_put/patch unknown.

roles.how: Map IdP groups to built-in or custom Userpilot roles per application; highest-privilege role wins when a user is in several groups; IdP-owned, hybrid or Userpilot-owned role management modes.

limitations.text: Requires SSO; once SCIM is on, SSO login is mandatory and SSO cannot be disabled until SCIM is disabled.
While SCIM is active, manual invites and CSV import of teammates are disabled.
The last remaining Account Owner is never removed by a sync.
Disabling SCIM leaves already-provisioned teammates with access.

scim.notes: SCIM is configured through a hosted setup portal from the Authentication page; the docs list the IdPs (Okta, Microsoft Entra ID and others) but publish no SCIM base URL, token type, endpoints or attribute list.

user_api.notes: Userpilot's HTTP API identifies end-users and companies of the customer's product and tracks events; the API reference index has no teammate, role or invite endpoints.

okta.notes: https://www.okta.com/integrations/userpilot/ returned 404; Userpilot's docs name Okta as a supported SSO and SCIM IdP via its setup portal.

fallbacks.notes: JIT (Enterprise, requires SSO over SAML or OIDC) creates teammates on first SSO login with a default role; CSV teammate import is on every plan.
